title: Validity, Extension and Rollover Terms of TimeBank Prepaid Service Hours Blocks
content:
For TimeBank Prepaid Service Hours, each block size fixes how long its hours may be drawn, whether its expiry may be extended for a fee, and whether its unused hours may roll into a new block.

| Figure | 10-Hour | 20-Hour | 40-Hour | 80-Hour | 160-Hour | 320-Hour |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Months from activation during which hours may be drawn | 6 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 18 |
| Expiry may be extended for a fee | no | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Months added by one extension | 0 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 6 | 6 |
| Extension fee, percent of remaining hours valued at the rate per block hour | 0 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 7.5 | 7.5 |
| Most extensions one block may receive | 0 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| Unused hours may roll into a new block bought before expiry | no | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Most hours that may roll over, percent of the expiring block's block hours | 0 | 25 | 25 | 50 | 50 | 50 |
| Days before the expiring block's expiry date from which a new block qualifies to receive its rollover | 0 | 60 | 60 | 60 | 90 | 90 |
| Receiving block must be the same size or larger | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Hours that already rolled over may roll over a second time | no | no | no | no | no | no |
| Unused hours refundable or convertible to credit | no | no | no | no | no | no |

## Reading the table

- The TimeBank 10-Hour Block can be neither extended nor rolled over; its zero figures for extension months, fee, extension count, rollover cap and rollover window follow from that.
- The rollover cap is a share of the expiring block's own block hours. A hypothetical 20-Hour Block at a 25 percent cap may roll at most 5 hours; a hypothetical 160-Hour Block at a 50 percent cap may roll at most 80 hours.
- No size refunds unused hours or converts them to credit against other services.
